also: look it up in the dictionary

evidence: M-O s.v. dictionary, lexicon, after Vives
terms.comment: Greek λεξικόν, a book of words; not in Lewis & Short. Vives uses it of a Greek–Latin dictionary (Morgan–Owens).

evidence: M-O s.v. dictionary, lexicon, after Vives
terms.comment: A book of dictiōnēs, words, and the word behind English dictionary; Traupman’s first word: id inquīre in dictiōnāriō, look it up in the dictionary (p. 33).

evidence: M-O s.v. dictionary, lexicon, after Vives
terms.comment: Vives’s word for the great Latin dictionaries of his day, Calepino’s and Perotti’s (Morgan–Owens).

terms.gloss: a glossary of old or rare words
terms.comment: A list of obsolete or foreign words with their meanings, not a dictionary of the whole language.

phrases.english: Look it up in the dictionary.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. dictionary, lexicon.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 29, 33, 34, 303, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
